study.question: Does the aligned/unit product gain depend on the normalization denominator derivative, or can the same forward scaling with a stopped norm retain or improve performance? The full-population validation leader r0005-normalized_aligned has AUC 0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19656340759133067 on 3,234,051 impressions, 159,437 positives. Its AUC gain over raw aligned is +0.0004876567525730 (Logloss -0.00012701821779649); crossed normalization gives only +0.0000139449288980 AUC and +0.0002459430732127 Logloss. The descriptive normalization-by-pairing interaction +0.0004737118236750 could reflect backward conditioning. First-512 unit norms cannot distinguish that explanation. The older raw corner also needs a same-body end-to-end bridge. This is an attribution experiment on an existing local improvement, not a claim that detached training will improve it.
study.hypothesis: Away from the fixed floor, full L2 normalization suppresses the radial product-gradient component. This projection contributes to the aligned normalization gain under the frozen recipe. For r=||p||>1e-3 and u=p/r, full local Jacobian is (I-u*u^T)/r, detached is I/r. Stopping only the norm derivative leaves identical common-state forward values but may degrade aligned AUC; an aligned-specific explanation predicts a more negative detached-minus-full effect for aligned than crossed. Below the floor both use constant-denominator derivative I/1e-3; no derivative claim is made at the clamp boundary. This is a hypothesis, not measured gradient evidence.

study.proposed_difference: Three prospectively registered standalone modules, ordered raw bridge, aligned detached candidate, crossed detached control. Only the new normalization_gradient=detached rule changes training arithmetic; detach is applied to the denominator after clamped square-root calculation, never to the numerator/history/whole product. Both detached arms have exactly the same class source and trainable capacity as the parent. Full-gradient unit corners and crossed/raw corner reuse verified round-5 ancestors. Retain registered seed 42; the interface supplies no seed-varying submission, so do not emulate seeds in model code. Do not run training here: host consumes proposal.json. Diagnostic additions are label-free same-state product/logit equality checks and mode flag, 58 scalars total, on the first 512 host rows under no_grad. They cannot measure training gradients. No optimizer, loss, masks, data, scorer or contract changes.
predictions: The raw bridge should reproduce r0004-same_field_replay aggregate/slice metrics if source-level equivalence transfers end-to-end; disagreement is an implementation finding and must be retained.

Under beneficial full-gradient projection, aligned detached-minus-full AUC is negative. Absolute AUC 0.0001 is a predeclared practical screening threshold, not an uncertainty interval or statistical equivalence margin.

If that projection is specifically useful to aligned fields, detached-minus-full AUC is more negative for aligned than crossed; report the full 2x2 table and interaction for both metrics. A general backward effect can occur without this interaction.

Parameter counts should remain 17,130,275 under identical host metadata; measured time/memory may differ due to backward graph and diagnostics. Report fixed data-pass comparisons and actual cost, not a claimed equal-compute frontier.
falsifiers: Detached aligned exceeding full aligned by >0.0001 AUC contradicts the directional useful-projection hypothesis for seed 42; preserve any Logloss tradeoff. Near-null does not prove no gradient effect.

Nonnegative gradient-by-pairing interaction contradicts the directional aligned-specific projection hypothesis; failure of the aligned/crossed gap under detached gradients weakens a forward-only alignment interpretation.

Detaching restores radial updates but retains inverse-norm scaling. Changed embedding norms alter other shared paths and later effective step sizes, so differences cannot be attributed exclusively to semantic field relevance or a single-step gradient component.
Adam state, checkpoint selection and nonconvex training mediate the intervention. Same-state forward identity does not imply equal learned checkpoints or deployment outputs.
